description: Two-panel mechanical-property figure for a duplex lightweight steel (Fe-30Mn-9Al-1C-1V-5Ni wt.%, per the abstract); no specimen label is printed on the panels. (a) Engineering stress (MPa, 0-1600, gridlines every 200) versus engineering strain (%, 0-14, ticks every 2): a red curve rises almost vertically to a plateau just above the 1200 MPa gridline, then increases slowly and nearly linearly to a peak just below the 1500 MPa gridline at roughly 12.5% strain, after which a dashed segment marks the abrupt drop to fracture. The inset is a grey SEM fractograph of the fracture surface, dominated by fine equiaxed dimples, with a white scale bar labelled 2 μm. (b) True stress and work-hardening rate (GPa, 0-8, ticks every 1) versus true strain (%, 0-12). A smooth black curve is true stress, rising steeply to about the 1 GPa level and then slowly to just above the 2 GPa gridline; a noisy red curve is the work-hardening rate, falling sharply (below zero) before climbing to a plateau near the 3-to-4 GPa level and then decaying slowly. Dashed vertical lines delimit three stages labelled I, II and III; an inset re-plots both curves over 0-5% true strain. Together the panels show the ultrahigh-strength, ductile response and its three-stage strain-hardening behaviour.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress (MPa) vs engineering strain (%) curve in red, from 0 to ~12.5% strain; it rises steeply to a plateau above 1200 MPa, then climbs slowly to a peak just under 1500 MPa and drops abruptly (dashed) at fracture. Inset: SEM fractograph of the fracture surface showing dimples, with a 2 μm scale bar.

True stress (black) and work-hardening rate (red, noisy) vs true strain (%), both on a 0-8 GPa axis. Vertical dashed lines at roughly 0.6%, 1%, 4.3% and ~11.7% strain delimit stages labelled I, II (work-hardening rate rising to a plateau near 3-4 GPa) and III (slow decay). Inset zooms the 0-5% true-strain range, showing the work-hardening rate dipping below zero before recovering.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an engineering stress-strain curve with engineering stress in MPa on a 0-1600 axis (gridlines every 200 MPa) and engineering strain in % on a 0-14 axis (ticks every 2%).

The red engineering stress-strain curve reaches a plateau just above the 1200 MPa gridline at about 1% strain, then rises slowly to a peak just below the 1500 MPa gridline at roughly 12.5% strain, followed by an abrupt dashed drop indicating fracture.
The inset of panel (a) is a grey SEM image of the fracture surface covered by fine dimples, with a white scale bar annotated 2 μm, indicating ductile fracture.
Panel (b) plots true stress and work-hardening rate on a shared axis of 0-8 GPa against true strain from 0 to 12% (major ticks every 2%).
In panel (b) the smooth black true-stress curve rises steeply to about the 1 GPa level at ~1% strain and then increases gradually to just above the 2 GPa gridline at ~12% strain.

The noisy red work-hardening-rate curve in panel (b) rises from near zero to a broad maximum lying between the 3 and 4 GPa gridlines at around 4% true strain, then decays slowly while remaining between the 2.5 and 3.5 GPa levels up to ~11.7% strain.
Four dashed vertical lines divide panel (b) into regions labelled I, II and III, with boundaries at roughly 0.6%, 1%, 4.3% and ~11.7% true strain.

The inset of panel (b) expands the 0-5% true-strain range on the same 0-8 GPa ordinate and shows the work-hardening rate falling sharply to below zero before recovering upward, while the true-stress curve saturates near 1 GPa.

The caption states that the figure reports tensile properties of the duplex lightweight steel, with (a) the engineering stress-strain curve and (b) the true stress-strain curve with its corresponding work-hardening rate curve.

The citing text states the yield strength is 1316 ± 16 MPa, the ultimate tensile strength is 1458 ± 11 MPa and the uniform elongation is 11.7 ± 1.2%; these numeric values are not printed anywhere on the figure panels.

The citing text describes three work-hardening stages: stage I (0-1%) with a sharp decrease to below zero, stage II (1-4.3%) with a rapid increase, and stage III (>4.3% true strain) where the rate decreases slowly but stays at 2.7-3.7 GPa.

The citing text attributes the stage II work-hardening rise to dislocation storage in austenite and B2 grains plus accumulation at austenite/B2 interfaces (forest and HDI hardening), and the stage III decay to dynamic recovery and dissolution of ordered domains.
The citing text states the SEM inset in Figure 4a shows a dimple-dominated fracture surface, indicating ductile fracture.
